notes: Four-lane parallel sweep (ai / bigtech+hardware+mobile / devtools+cloud / security) covering 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26. All lanes hit routine EGRESS_BLOCKED on org-domain WebFetch (anthropic.com, blog.google, dataprotection.ie, blogs.windows.com, kubernetes.io, azure.microsoft.com, cisa.gov, bleepingcomputer.com, iclr.cc, neurips.cc) and worked from WebSearch results instead. A quiet-ish day: most lane candidates cross-checked against the full corpus turned out to already be filed accurately (OpenAI DevDay 2026, Geneva AI Summit 2027, Kubernetes 1.36 EOL, gpt-5.4-cyber retirement, npm bypass-2FA token retirement, Google Play US alt-billing/link-out fees, CES 2027, MWC Barcelona 2027) so were not resubmitted. Genuinely new: Anthropic's Claude computing a nine-loop scattering amplitude (verified by the prior human record-holder), an $11.6B Anthropic-Akamai compute deal, Google's Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar going GA, a €403M Irish DPC fine against Google over location-data GDPR violations, new Surface Pro/Laptop hardware with a firm on-sale date, an Istio 1.29 EOL date, a Deno 2.9 LTS end-of-maintenance date, an Azure Monitor Container Insights legacy-table retirement, a Google Cloud SDK Snap package deprecation, a confirmed $351.6M Bitget crypto hack attributed to North Korea-linked actors, and a disclosed (already patched) 'SalesBleed' zero-click Salesforce Agentforce vulnerability chain. Also resolved two standing corpus problems this run (see concerns): the Veradigm breach is now company-confirmed via SEC 8-K rather than only a ransomware gang's unverified claim, and two long-standing duplicate/stale entries were cleaned up via the schema's 'superseded' status. A few stale (2-4 day old) items surfaced by the lanes (a federal 'Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act' bill introduction, an Alibaba Qwen-Audio price cut, a Microsoft/DARPA quantum-computing access announcement) were deliberately left out per the no-backfill rule and the 'would an engineer want this on their calendar' bar.
concerns: Fixed a standing duplicate: data/events/2027-02.json carried two near-identical entries for the same OpenAI transcription-model retirement on 2027-02-26 ('...whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe family' vs '...Whisper-1 and GPT-4o transcription models') that never merged because their title-token overlap (5/9 = 0.56) sits just under src/lib/id.ts's 0.6 threshold. Superseded the weaker, single-sourced 'family' entry in favor of the fuller, two-sourced 'transcription models' one by reusing its exact title/org/date so the apply script's id-match hits it directly.

Fixed a stale/wrong date left un-superseded: 'AWS Lambda blocks updates to Node.js 20.x functions' (filed at 2026-09-30) was corrected in effect by two later runs' 2027-02/2027-03 entries, but the original wrong-dated row was never itself marked superseded and was still live on the calendar showing an incorrect September 2026 date. Superseded it this run (exact title/org/date reused for the id-match) rather than filing a fourth overlapping entry.

The Veradigm correction reuses the existing entry's exact stale title ('Ransomware group sets leak deadline for Veradigm patient data') verbatim to guarantee the apply script's token-overlap dedupe merges into the existing row rather than filing a contradictory second entry — the title no longer describes what's actually being reported (a company-confirmed SEC 8-K breach disclosure, not just a gang's unverified leak-deadline claim.) Same trick used for the two supersede entries above. If a future run wonders why these titles don't match their content, this is why.

'Google Cloud SDK Snap package deprecated' (2026-09-29) rests on a single, non-date-specific source (Google's general release-notes index page, not a direct fetch) — filed at 'expected' rather than 'confirmed' for that reason; worth a direct-fetch check once cloud.google.com is reachable.

Standing unresolved items re-checked this run, no change: ST Engineering MetaEncryptor ransomware claim remains unconfirmed by the company; Huawei Mate 90's launch date remains Huawei-unconfirmed (still only pattern-matched leak reporting pointing to Sept 29); the Azure AKS VMAS auto-migration date conflict (2025 vs 2026 across secondary sources) remains unresolved; ICML 2027's exact dates remain unpublished by icml.cc (one aggregator claims July 2027 in South America but this could not be corroborated and may be conflating an unrelated conference of the same acronym).
